transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-12-20
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Leah Martinez (Redwood AE), Dimitri Koh (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Logan Price (Redwood CSM); Aisha Patel (CISO - Corvus Health), Mark Reynolds (Head Infra), Sara Kim (Legal), Ethan Wu (Platform)

Summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Quick security posture discovery focused on hosted vs dedicated vs private options. Main topics: SOC2/ISO status, SSO/SAML and SSO integration, RBAC and audit logs, encryption (customer-managed keys / KMS, HSM), data residency and retention policies. Customer concerned about PHI handling and keys control; interested in private deployment but wants pricing and benchmark data.

Topics: SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, data retention, VPC/private deployment, Dedicated capacity, key management, incident response

Transcript:
[00:00] Leah (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros, then we can jump into security posture. I'm Leah from Redwood, AE.
[00:10] Aisha (CISO - Corvus): Hi, Aisha here, CISO. We handle HIPAA-adjacent data, so security is top of mind.
[00:15] Mark (Infra): Mark, infra lead, will be focused on networking and deployment questions.
[00:20] Leah: Great. Dimitri and Priya from our SE team are on to handle technical questions. Dimitri want to say hi?
[00:26] Dimitri (Redwood SE): Hey all, yeah hi. I'll cover deployment, key mgmt, and audit logs.
[00:30] [00:30] Ethan (Platform): Ethan, platform, mostly ops questions.
[00:33] Leah: Cool. So high level, are you evaluating Hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, or Private (VPC/on-prem)?
[00:40] Aisha: We're exploring all three, but leaning toward Private because of PHI concerns and our contracts. We need strong guarantees around key control and auditability.
[00:50] Leah: Totally understand. Quick housekeeping: we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certifications, we can share the attestations. We also support customer-managed keys via KMS and HSM integrations for Private and Dedicated.
[01:05] Aisha: That helps. For Hosted, do you support BYOK?
[01:08] Dimitri: Hosted currently supports envelope encryption with keys managed by Redwood, and we offer bring-your-own-key for Dedicated and Private deployments. Our hosted offering can do some customer key configurations via cloud KMS integrations, but it's not the same as fully customer-controlled HSM in a VPC.
[01:23] Mark: For our legal team, we need to know retention windows for logs and transcripts. Also audit logs - who can access them?
[01:30] Priya (Redwood SE): Audit logs are available in the Console. We can export to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) or deliver via secure S3. Access is role-based; we support RBAC and integration with SSO/SAML for provisioning.
[01:42] Sara (Legal): We need to make sure audit logs are tamper-evident and retained for at least seven years in our case. Is that possible?
[01:50] Dimitri: Seven years is long but feasible. We usually ship logs to customer-managed storage for long-term retention, that meets the tamper-evidence requirement if you use object lock or equivalent. For on-prem/private deployments you can set retention policies on your side too.
[02:05] Aisha: And encryption at rest for stored transcripts? If an employee leaves, can we rotate keys and invalidate previous access?
[02:13] Dimitri: Yes - with customer-managed KMS/HSM you control key rotation. We support key rotation and key revocation semantics; you can rotate keys which will require re-encrypting data depending on your setup, or you can maintain separate key versions.
[02:25] Leah: Quick note: some of the language in our docs might say "K-V cash" in transcripts - sorry our transcriber messes up KV cache sometimes.
[02:33] (laughter)
[02:35] Ethan: On the topic of data in transit between Redwood control plane and private nodes - for Private deployment, can control plane metadata cross the public internet? We need an air-gapped or fully VPC peered solution for compliance.
[02:47] Dimitri: For Private we offer a customer-controlled control plane option where connections are via private link or VPC peering. For air-gapped we have an on-prem package. We should plan a technical deep dive to show the exact topology.
[03:05] Mark: If we go Dedicated (reserved GPUs) what assurances do we get about noisy neighbor and tenancy?
[03:12] Priya: Dedicated gives isolated GPU pools for only your workloads; single-tenant behaviour. You get predictable throughput and SLA-backed latency targets. For extra isolation you can opt for Private.
[03:23] Aisha: Incident response: what's your process and SLAs for security incidents?
[03:30] Leah: We have an incident response playbook and page in the vendor security docs. We notify customers per contract and provide post-incident reports. For Dedicated and Private we offer more direct support channels and faster escalation.
[03:45] Sara: Do you provide SOC 2 audit logs showing access to customer data by Redwood staff? We need demonstrable proof that only authorized roles accessed things.
[03:54] Dimitri: Yes, we log operator actions. The console and audit trail include role-based accesses, with timestamps and requester identity. We can supply redacted examples and mapping to roles.
[04:06] Aisha: Who holds the encryption keys in Hosted? If Redwood holds keys, what's the legal boundary for subpoenas?
[04:13] Leah: When Redwood manages keys, we have legal team processes for responding to lawful requests and we surface those in our contracts. For customers that need to avoid Redwood having key access, Dedicated or Private with BYOK/HSM is recommended.
[04:26] Ethan: For telemetry and billing, what PII or metadata leaves our environment?
[04:30] Dimitri: We collect usage metrics at token and route granularity for billing and SLO purposes. We can redact or minimize data in logs; we also support sending telemetry to your own observability stack.
[04:40] Mark: On SSO, we use OKTA and SCIM for user provisioning. How does RBAC integrate?
[04:46] Priya: We integrate SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC maps to your IdP groups; you can control Console roles (admin, deployer, viewer) and finer-grained policies are available for audit/log access.
[04:58] Sara: We need MFA enforcement and log of admin actions.
[05:02] Dimitri: MFA is enforced via your IdP; admin actions are logged in the audit trail with identity from SAML assertion.
[05:10] Aisha: What about model data retention - input prompts, outputs, and embeddings? We cannot retain PHI for more than X days per our policy.
[05:20] Leah: We support configurable retention policies. For Hosted we can set auto deletion windows; Dedicated and Private give you full control. For embeddings, we recommend hashing or tokenizing sensitive fields and controlling retention on your side for maximum compliance.
[05:34] Ethan: If we need to run red-team style evals and keep prompts for repro, can we limit exposure to a small team and keep logs audited?
[05:42] Priya: Yes - you can configure role-based access and restrict log exports. We can also provide segregated buckets for those logs with separate IAM controls.
[05:52] Mark: Performance question tied to security: does enabling encryption or private networking impact latency?
[05:57] Dimitri: Very slightly. Using customer-managed KMS calls for key unwrap adds a few ms on first call but the runtime uses KV cache to keep keys in memory for inference; private networking (VPC peering) adds minimal network hops but predictable latency. We'll show numbers in the technical deep dive.
[06:14] Aisha: About compliance artifacts - we need a list of SOC2 controls mapped to your implementation and a contact for whitepaper review.
[06:22] Leah: I'll send SOC2 Type II report and an implementation mapping doc. Dimitri will provide architecture and controls mapping for Private/Dedicated.
[06:31] Sara: For contract language - need clauses for data residency, encryption, and forensic logs. Does Redwood support specific contractual addenda?
[06:38] Leah: Yes, for enterprise we have addenda for data processing, residency, and encryption. We can loop in legal to share templates.
[06:45] Ethan: One more technical nit: KV cache and session persistence - if we run multi-tenant workloads, do you shard KV cache per customer and is it persisted?
[06:55] Dimitri: Yes, KV cache is per-model and per-session; we isolate per-tenant and don't persist sensitive session state beyond configured retention. Caches are in-memory for performance and can be flushed on demand.
[07:08] [07:08] Aisha: Any known gaps for HIPAA specifically?
[07:12] Leah: We have customers in regulated spaces; HIPAA compliance is largely a function of deployment and contractual controls. We'll coordinate with our compliance team to map controls.
[07:22] Mark: For Private on-prem deployment, what's the install footprint and maintenance window?
[07:27] Dimitri: On-prem package includes inference runtime, a lightweight control agent, and operator docs. We'll provide sizing based on your request (number of concurrent requests, seq lengths). Maintenance windows are customer-configurable; by default we recommend scheduled maintenance with canary nodes.
[07:42] Sara: Is there attestation that Redwood staff can't access raw customer prompts for hosted?
[07:48] Leah: We can provide attestation language and describe the internal controls; for absolute assurance BYOK on Dedicated/Private is the path.
[07:58] Ethan: One more: SIEM integration - you said Splunk and Datadog. Are the log schemas documented?
[08:03] Priya: Yes, we have log schema docs and sample events. We'll share them.
[08:08] Mark: Let's talk timeline - we aim to start a pilot in Q1. We need bench numbers and security docs before procurement.
[08:15] Leah: Sounds good. We'll send the docs and propose a technical deep dive next week.
[08:20] Aisha: For the benchmark, can you remove any model telemetry leaving our environment and just provide latency/throughput numbers?
[08:26] Dimitri: We can run an isolated benchmark inside a Private pilot or send aggregated metrics only. We'll make sure telemetry minimization is an option.
[08:36] [08:36] Recap and next steps:
Leah: Recap - Leah will send SOC2, ISO summaries, security whitepaper; Dimitri will share Private deployment architecture, log schema, and benchmark plan. We'll schedule a technical deep dive for VPC/on-prem specifics and a demo of RBAC/SSO. Customer will list the compliance artifacts they need and confirm retention windows.
[08:58] Aisha: That works. Thanks everyone.
[09:02] Leah: Thanks all, we'll follow up via email with links to docs and calendar invites.

End of transcript.
